standard_text: Multiplication and division facts to 100 (introductory computational strategies)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on multiplication and division facts to 100: arrays, skip counting, doubles, near facts, fact families, missing factors and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the BC curriculum and useful for the FSA.
key_big: Use a fact you know to find one you don’t: 6 × 7 = 6 × 6 + 6 = 42.
key_sub: The 4s are double the 2s, and the 5s are half of the 10s. Every multiplication fact gives division facts: 7 × 8 = 56, so 56 ÷ 8 = 7 and 56 ÷ 7 = 8.
body_html:
Multiplication means equal groups

4 × 6 means 4 groups of 6. Skip count by 6s: 6, 12, 18, 24. So 4 × 6 = 24. You can multiply in any order: 6 × 4 = 24 too. In Grade 4 you work with all facts up to 10 × 10 = 100.

Strategies for harder facts

StrategyHow it worksExample
DoublesThe 4s are double the 2s4 × 7: 14 + 14 = 28
HalvesThe 5s are half of the 10s5 × 8: half of 80 = 40
Near fact: one more groupUse a fact you know, then add one group6 × 7 = 6 × 6 + 6 = 42
Near fact: one group lessThe 9s are the 10s take away one group9 × 7 = 70 − 7 = 63
Example

8 × 6 = ?

8 is double 4. 4 × 6 = 24, and 24 + 24 = 48.

Answer: 48

Every fact gives division facts

Division is the opposite of multiplication. 7, 8 and 56 make a fact family: 7 × 8 = 56, 8 × 7 = 56, 56 ÷ 7 = 8 and 56 ÷ 8 = 7. A division fact starts with the biggest number.

Division

63 ÷ 9 = ?

Think: 9 × ? = 63. 9 × 7 = 63.

Answer: 7

Missing factor

? × 6 = 54

Think: 54 ÷ 6. 6 × 9 = 54.

Answer: 9

Word problem

A BC Ferries car deck has 6 rows with 9 cars in each row. How many cars is that?

6 rows of 9: 6 × 9 = 54.

Answer: 54 cars

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding instead of multiplying: 6 × 9 = 15× means groups of: 6 groups of 9 = 54
Mixing up 7 × 8 = 54Say 5, 6, 7, 8: 56 = 7 × 8. (54 is 6 × 9.)
Near fact: 6 × 7 = 36 + 1 = 37Add a whole group of 6: 36 + 6 = 42
Dividing the wrong way: 8 ÷ 56 = 7Start with the biggest number: 56 ÷ 8 = 7

faq.q: What multiplication facts should a Grade 4 student know in BC?
faq.a: The BC Mathematics Curriculum asks Grade 4 students to work with multiplication and division facts to 100, using strategies such as doubling, halving and near facts. Many students know the 2s, 5s and 10s well and are building up the 3s, 4s and harder facts like 7 × 8.

faq.q: Is multiplication on the Grade 4 FSA?
faq.a: The FSA numeracy section is based on the BC curriculum, so it can include multiplication and division, often inside word problems. Knowing the facts quickly leaves more time to think about each problem.

faq.q: What is a near fact in Grade 4 math?
faq.a: A near fact uses a fact you already know to find one next to it. For example, 6 × 6 = 36, so 6 × 7 is one more group of 6: 36 + 6 = 42.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn multiplication and division facts at home?
faq.a: Practise a few facts each day and ask for the matching division fact too, such as 4 × 8 = 32 and 32 ÷ 8 = 4. Everyday things like packs of hockey cards or rows of cars make the facts real.

sets.title: Facts with arrays and skip counting: 2s, 5s, 10s, 3s and 4s

items.q: How many counters are there in all?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 3. 4 × 3 = 12. 7 is 4 + 3, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: How many counters are there in all?
items.e: There are 6 groups of 4. 6 × 4 = 24. 10 is 6 + 4, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 2 rows with 9 dots in each row. 2 × 9 = 18. 11 is 2 + 9, which adds instead of multiplies.
There are 5 rows with 7 dots in each row. 5 × 7 = 35. 12 is 5 + 7, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 8 dots in each row. 3 × 8 = 24. 11 is 3 + 8, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Which number sentence matches this array?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 6 dots in each row, so it shows 4 × 6 = 24. 4 + 6 adds the numbers instead of multiplying.

items.q: Which number sentence matches this array?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 9 dots in each row, so it shows 3 × 9 = 27. 3 + 9 adds the numbers instead of multiplying.

items.q:
Skip count by 2s. What comes next?
12, 14, 16, ?
items.e: Each number is 2 more than the one before: 16 + 2 = 18. So 2 × 9 = 18.

items.q:
Skip count by 5s. What comes next?
30, 35, 40, ?
items.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before: 40 + 5 = 45. So 5 × 9 = 45.

items.q:
Skip count by 10s. What comes next?
60, 70, 80, ?
items.e: Each number is 10 more than the one before: 80 + 10 = 90. So 10 × 9 = 90.

items.q:
Skip count by 3s. What comes next?
12, 15, 18, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 18 + 3 = 21. So 3 × 7 = 21.

items.q:
Skip count by 4s. What comes next?
20, 24, 28, ?
items.e: Each number is 4 more than the one before: 28 + 4 = 32. So 4 × 8 = 32.

items.q: Which fact does this number line show?
items.e: There are 7 jumps of 3 from 0 to 21: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21. So 7 × 3 = 21.
Half of the 10s: 10 × 7 = 70, and half of 70 is 35.
6 tens make 60. So 6 × 10 = 60.
3 groups of 6: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18. Or 2 × 6 = 12, plus one more 6: 18.
Double, then double again: 2 × 9 = 18, and double 18 is 36.
Double, then double again: 2 × 7 = 14, and double 14 is 28.
3 groups of 9: 9 + 9 + 9 = 27. Or 2 × 9 = 18, plus one more 9: 27.

sets.title: Strategies: doubles, halves and near facts

items.q: 2 × 7 = 14. Double it to find 4 × 7.
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 7 is double 2 × 7: 14 + 14 = 28. 21 is only 3 groups of 7.

items.q: 2 × 6 = 12. Double it to find 4 × 6.
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 6 is double 2 × 6: 12 + 12 = 24. 18 is only 3 groups of 6.

items.q: 2 × 9 = 18. Double it to find 4 × 9.
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 9 is double 2 × 9: 18 + 18 = 36. 27 is only 3 groups of 9.

items.q: 2 × 8 = 16. Double it to find 4 × 8.
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 8 is double 2 × 8: 16 + 16 = 32. 24 is only 3 groups of 8.

items.q: 10 × 8 = 80. Use it to find 5 × 8.
items.e: 5 is half of 10, so 5 × 8 is half of 10 × 8. Half of 80 is 40. 75 takes away only 5.

items.q: 10 × 7 = 70. Use it to find 5 × 7.
items.e: 5 is half of 10, so 5 × 7 is half of 10 × 7. Half of 70 is 35. 65 takes away only 5.

items.q: 10 × 9 = 90. Use it to find 5 × 9.
items.e: 5 is half of 10, so 5 × 9 is half of 10 × 9. Half of 90 is 45. 85 takes away only 5.

items.q: 5 × 6 = 30. Use it to find 10 × 6.
items.e: 10 is double 5, so 10 × 6 is double 5 × 6: 30 + 30 = 60. 35 adds 5 instead of doubling.

items.q: 6 × 6 = 36. Use the picture to find 7 × 6.
items.e: 7 rows of 6 is 6 rows of 6 plus one more row of 6: 36 + 6 = 42. 37 adds 1, not one more group of 6.

items.q: 7 × 7 = 49. Use it to find 7 × 8.
items.e: 7 × 8 is one more group of 7 than 7 × 7: 49 + 7 = 56. Add a whole group of 7, not 1.

items.q: 8 × 8 = 64. Use it to find 8 × 9.
items.e: 8 × 9 is one more group of 8 than 8 × 8: 64 + 8 = 72. Add a whole group of 8, not 1.

items.q: 9 × 5 = 45. Use it to find 9 × 6.
items.e: 9 × 6 is one more group of 9 than 9 × 5: 45 + 9 = 54. Add a whole group of 9, not 1.

items.q: 5 × 8 = 40. Use it to find 6 × 8.
items.e: 6 × 8 is one more group of 8 than 5 × 8: 40 + 8 = 48. Add a whole group of 8, not 1.

items.q: 10 × 7 = 70. Use it to find 9 × 7.
items.e: 9 groups is one group less than 10 groups. 10 × 7 = 70, then take away one 7: 70 − 7 = 63. Take away 7, not 1.

items.q: 10 × 6 = 60. Use it to find 9 × 6.
items.e: 9 groups is one group less than 10 groups. 10 × 6 = 60, then take away one 6: 60 − 6 = 54. Take away 6, not 1.

items.q: Which is a good way to work out 6 × 7?
items.e: 6 × 7 is 7 groups of 6. That is 6 groups of 6 plus one more 6: 36 + 6 = 42.

items.q: Which is the same as 8 × 6?
Which is the same as 4 × 9?
Which number sentence is true?
Only one of these number sentences is correct. Which one?
items.e: 4 × 7 is double 2 × 7: 14 + 14 = 28. 11 adds instead of multiplies, 21 is only 3 sevens, and 24 is 4 × 6.

sets.title: Related division facts and fact families

items.q: 15 counters are put into groups of 3. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the groups: there are 5 groups of 3. 15 ÷ 3 = 5. Check: 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: 28 counters are put into groups of 4. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the groups: there are 7 groups of 4. 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Check: 7 × 4 = 28.

items.q: 6 × 8 = 48. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 6, 8 and 48 make a fact family. 6 × 8 = 48, so 48 ÷ 6 = 8 and 48 ÷ 8 = 6. Division starts with the biggest number, 48.

items.q: 7 × 9 = 63. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 7, 9 and 63 make a fact family. 7 × 9 = 63, so 63 ÷ 7 = 9 and 63 ÷ 9 = 7. Division starts with the biggest number, 63.

items.q: 4 × 7 = 28. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 4, 7 and 28 make a fact family. 4 × 7 = 28, so 28 ÷ 4 = 7 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4. Division starts with the biggest number, 28.

items.q: Which fact is in the same fact family as 3 × 9 = 27?
items.e: The fact family for 3, 9 and 27 is 3 × 9 = 27, 9 × 3 = 27, 27 ÷ 3 = 9 and 27 ÷ 9 = 3. 9 ÷ 27 is turned around: division starts with the biggest number.

items.q: Which fact is in the same fact family as 8 × 7 = 56?
items.e: The fact family for 8, 7 and 56 is 8 × 7 = 56, 7 × 8 = 56, 56 ÷ 8 = 7 and 56 ÷ 7 = 8. 7 ÷ 56 is turned around: division starts with the biggest number.

items.q: Which fact is not in the fact family for 4, 6 and 24?
items.e: 4 × 6 = 24, 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4 are all in the family. 6 ÷ 24 = 4 divides the wrong way: start with the biggest number, 24.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 49 ÷ 7?
items.e: 49 ÷ 7 asks: 7 times what makes 49? 7 × 7 = 49, so 49 ÷ 7 = 7.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 72 ÷ 8?
items.e: 72 ÷ 8 asks: 8 times what makes 72? 8 × 9 = 72, so 72 ÷ 8 = 9.

items.q: Which multiplication fact checks 45 ÷ 5 = 9?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the number you divided by: 9 × 5 = 45. Subtracting 5 once does not undo dividing by 5.

items.q: How many 3s make 27?
items.e: 27 ÷ 3 = ? Skip count by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27. That is 9 jumps. 24 is 27 − 3, which subtracts only one 3.
Ask: 3 times what makes 24? 24 ÷ 3 = 8. Check: 3 × 8 = 24, so ? = 8.
Ask: 4 times what makes 36? 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Check: 4 × 9 = 36, so ? = 9.
Ask: 6 times what makes 42? 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Check: 6 × 7 = 42, so ? = 7.
Ask: 7 times what makes 49? 49 ÷ 7 = 7. Check: 7 × 7 = 49, so ? = 7.
Ask: 8 times what makes 32? 32 ÷ 8 = 4. Check: 8 × 4 = 32, so ? = 4.
Ask: 9 times what makes 54? 54 ÷ 9 = 6. Check: 9 × 6 = 54, so ? = 6.
Ask: what times 3 makes 18? 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Check: 6 × 3 = 18, so ? = 6.
Ask: what times 7 makes 56? 56 ÷ 7 = 8. Check: 8 × 7 = 56, so ? = 8.
Ask: what times 8 makes 72? 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Check: 9 × 8 = 72, so ? = 9.
Ask: what times 6 makes 30? 30 ÷ 6 = 5. Check: 5 × 6 = 30, so ? = 5.
Division undoes multiplication, so multiply back: ? = 7 × 4 = 28. Check: 28 ÷ 4 = 7.
Division undoes multiplication, so multiply back: ? = 8 × 6 = 48. Check: 48 ÷ 6 = 8.
Division undoes multiplication, so multiply back: ? = 3 × 9 = 27. Check: 27 ÷ 9 = 3.

items.q: The jumps go from 0 to 24. Fill in: ? × 4 = 24
items.e: Count the jumps: there are 6 jumps of 4. 6 × 4 = 24, so ? = 6.

items.q: The jumps go from 0 to 24. Fill in: ? × 3 = 24
items.e: Count the jumps: there are 8 jumps of 3. 8 × 3 = 24, so ? = 8.

items.q: An array has 6 rows and 42 dots. How many dots are in each row?
items.e: 6 × ? = 42. 42 ÷ 6 = 7, so each row has 7 dots. 36 is 42 − 6, which subtracts instead of dividing.

items.q:
Which number makes both true?
4 × ? = 28 and 28 ÷ ? = 4
items.e: 4 × 7 = 28 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4. They are in the same fact family, so ? = 7. 24 is 28 − 4.

sets.title: Word problems: ferries, hockey cards and field trips

items.q: This is part of a BC Ferries car deck. There are 6 rows with 9 cars in each row. How many cars is that?
items.e: 6 rows of 9: 6 × 9 = 54. 15 is 6 + 9, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Liam buys 6 packs of hockey cards. Each pack has 8 cards. How many cards does he get?
items.e: 6 packs of 8: 6 × 8 = 48. 5 × 8 = 40, plus one more 8 is 48. 14 is 6 + 8.

items.q: 54 cars wait for the ferry to Nanaimo. Each row on the car deck holds 9 cars. How many rows do the cars fill?
items.e: 54 ÷ 9 = ? 9 × 6 = 54, so the cars fill 6 rows. 45 is 54 − 9, which takes away only one row.

items.q: On this car deck, 5 rows have 7 cars each. The last row has only 3 cars. How many cars are there in all?
items.e: 5 full rows: 5 × 7 = 35. Add the last row: 35 + 3 = 38. 42 counts the last row as full.

items.q: Binder pages hold 9 hockey cards each. Nadia has 63 cards. How many pages can she fill?
items.e: 63 ÷ 9 = ? 9 × 7 = 63, so she fills 7 pages. 54 is 63 − 9.

items.q: Ryan has 4 Vancouver Canucks cards. His cousin has 6 times as many. How many Canucks cards does the cousin have?
items.e: 6 times as many as 4 means 6 × 4 = 24. 10 is 6 + 4, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Simran puts 32 hockey cards into 4 equal piles. How many cards are in each pile?
items.e: 32 ÷ 4 = ? 4 × 8 = 32, so each pile has 8 cards. 28 is 32 − 4.

items.q: Wei buys 3 packs of hockey cards with 9 cards in each pack. He gives 5 cards to a friend. How many cards does he have left?
items.e: First 3 × 9 = 27. Then 27 − 5 = 22. 27 forgets the 5 cards given away.

items.q: Hockey cards cost $3 a pack. Owen has $27. How many packs can he buy?
items.e: 27 ÷ 3 = ? 3 × 9 = 27, so he can buy 9 packs. 81 is 27 × 3, which multiplies instead of divides.

items.q: A Grade 4 class goes on a SkyTrain field trip. 9 students sit in each of 4 cars. How many students is that?
45 students walk in the Terry Fox Run in groups of 5. How many groups are there?
items.e: 45 ÷ 5 = ? 5 × 9 = 45, so there are 9 groups.

items.q: A chairlift at Whistler carries 4 skiers on each chair. How many skiers ride on 8 chairs?
items.e: 8 × 4 = 32. Double 8 is 16, double 16 is 32. 12 is 8 + 4.

items.q: 24 students go canoeing. 3 students sit in each canoe. How many canoes do they need?
items.e: 24 ÷ 3 = ? 3 × 8 = 24, so they need 8 canoes. 72 is 24 × 3, which multiplies instead of divides.

items.q: An orchard in the Okanagan packs apples in trays of 6. How many apples fit in 7 trays?
Mateo plants cedar seedlings in 8 rows. Each row has 7 seedlings. How many seedlings is that?
A lacrosse tournament in Burnaby has 7 teams. Each team has 10 players. How many players is that?
Chloe sees 3 bald eagles at each of 6 stops along the Squamish River. How many eagles is that?
items.e: 6 stops with 3 eagles: 6 × 3 = 18. 9 is 6 + 3.

items.q: Noah and his 2 friends share 24 crackers equally on a hike. How many crackers does each person get?
items.e: Noah and 2 friends is 3 people. 24 ÷ 3 = 8. 12 shares between only 2 people and forgets Noah.

items.q: Sofia has 7 packs of 10 hockey cards. Ethan has 8 packs of 8 cards. How many more cards does Sofia have?
items.e: Sofia: 7 × 10 = 70. Ethan: 8 × 8 = 64. 70 − 64 = 6. 134 adds the two totals instead of finding the difference.

items.q: A Kamloops school buys 9 boxes of markers. Each box has 8 markers. How many markers is that?
